name: serverless-anomaly-detection-system

ground_truth.threatName: Unauthorized Access to Kinesis Data Stream

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could use stolen credentials or exploit overly permissive IAM roles to access the Kinesis stream, potentially reading sensitive data or injecting malicious records.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker with compromised Lambda credentials could modify the data stream to inject false anomalies or suppress real ones.

recommendations.description: Implement strict IAM policies following the principle of least privilege
recommendations.implementationDetails: Review and restrict IAM roles to minimum required permissions. Use resource-level permissions and condition statements in IAM policies.
Enable CloudWatch detailed monitoring for Kinesis streams, set up alerts for unusual access patterns, and use AWS CloudTrail for API activity logging.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Kinesis streams support AWS KMS encryption which is currently enabled. Consider implementing additional VPC endpoints for Kinesis to restrict access to specific VPCs.

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could exploit misconfigured S3 bucket permissions or compromised credentials to modify or replace ML model artifacts.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker uploads a malicious model that deliberately misclassifies anomalies, causing the system to miss critical alerts.

recommendations.description: Implement versioning and integrity checks for model artifacts
recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable S3 versioning (already configured), implement checksums for model files, and use AWS Macie for sensitive data discovery.
Implement S3 Object Lock for model artifacts, use AWS KMS customer managed keys, and enable S3 access logging.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: The S3 bucket is configured with encryption and public access blocking, but consider implementing S3 Object Lock and additional monitoring through AWS Macie.

mitreATT&CK: T1562.001 - Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers might exploit poor input validation or environment variable handling to execute arbitrary code within Lambda functions.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker injects malicious code through specially crafted input data that exploits string evaluation or deserialization vulnerabilities.

recommendations.description: Implement robust input validation and sanitization
recommendations.implementationDetails: Add strict input validation for all Lambda function inputs, implement JSON schema validation, and avoid dangerous JavaScript functions like eval().
Configure IAM authentication for Lambda function URLs and implement request signing for direct invocations.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Lambda execution roles follow least privilege, but consider implementing AWS Lambda layer for shared security controls and input validation.

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could exploit overly permissive IAM policies or application-level vulnerabilities to access or modify sensitive data in DynamoDB.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker uses a compromised Lambda function to scan the DynamoDB table and extract historical anomaly data.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use IAM policy conditions to restrict access based on attributes, implement DynamoDB fine-grained access control, and enable server-side encryption with AWS KMS.
Enable DynamoDB Streams for change tracking, implement CloudWatch alarms for suspicious access patterns, and use AWS Config for compliance monitoring.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: DynamoDB point-in-time recovery is enabled for prod environment, but consider implementing additional encryption and access logging.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could exploit client-side vulnerabilities, manipulate API calls, or perform cross-site scripting attacks against the web interface.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker injects malicious JavaScript through a cross-site scripting vulnerability, stealing user session tokens.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure security headers in CloudFront, implement strict Content Security Policy, and enable AWS WAF for additional protection.
Implement SRI for external resources, use AWS Cognito for authentication, and enable CloudFront access logging.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: CloudFront is configured with TLS 1.2 and access logging, but consider implementing AWS WAF and Cognito for additional security.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could overwhelm the SageMaker endpoint with requests or attempt to poison the model through carefully crafted inputs.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker floods the SageMaker endpoint with requests, causing delays in anomaly detection and potential missed alerts.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure auto-scaling for the endpoint, implement request throttling, and set up detailed CloudWatch metrics for endpoint performance.
Implement input validation for model requests, configure VPC endpoints for SageMaker, and enable model monitoring for drift detection.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: SageMaker endpoint is configured with basic monitoring, but consider implementing VPC endpoints and model monitoring capabilities.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could attempt to suppress legitimate alerts or generate false alerts by manipulating the SNS topic or compromising the notification Lambda.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker with compromised credentials modifies SNS subscriptions to prevent alerts from reaching security teams.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure strict IAM policies for SNS topic access, implement message authentication, and enable SNS encryption.
Implement multiple notification channels, configure dead-letter queues for failed notifications, and enable detailed logging.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: SNS topics are configured with basic access controls, but consider implementing encryption and DLQ for failed messages.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could modify CloudWatch alarms, delete logs, or disable monitoring to hide malicious activities.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker with elevated privileges disables CloudWatch alarms and deletes logs to hide their activities.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable CloudWatch logs encryption, implement log retention policies, and use AWS CloudTrail for API activity monitoring.
Configure CloudWatch Synthetics for endpoint monitoring, implement cross-account logging, and use AWS Config for compliance monitoring.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: CloudWatch alarms are configured for basic metrics, but consider implementing advanced monitoring and cross-account logging.

#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""
AWS Serverless Real-Time Anomaly Detection Architecture Diagram
This script generates a high-resolution architecture diagram showing the components
and relationships in a serverless anomaly detection system on AWS.
"""

# Core diagram components
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge

# End-user devices
from diagrams.generic.device import Mobile

# AWS Analytics services
from diagrams.aws.analytics import KinesisDataStreams

# AWS Compute services
from diagrams.aws.compute import Lambda

# AWS Database services
from diagrams.aws.database import Dynamodb

# AWS Machine Learning services
from diagrams.aws.ml import SagemakerModel

# AWS Integration services
from diagrams.aws.integration import SNS

# AWS Management services
from diagrams.aws.management import Cloudwatch

# AWS Storage services
from diagrams.aws.storage import S3

# AWS Network services
from diagrams.aws.network import CloudFront

# AWS Mobile services
from diagrams.aws.mobile import Amplify

# AWS Security services
from diagrams.aws.security import IAM

# Error handling for diagram generation
import sys

# Diagram configuration with enhanced visual attributes
graph_attr = {
    "fontsize": "45",
    "bgcolor": "white",
    "splines": "ortho",
    "pad": "0.5",        # Reduced from 2.0
    "nodesep": "0.8",    # Reduced from 1.2
    "ranksep": "1.0",    # Reduced from 1.5
    "concentrate": "true",
    "labeldistance": "1.0",  # Added to control label distance
    "labelangle": "0",       # Added to control label angle
    "overlap": "false"       # Added to prevent overlap
}


# Node attribute configuration
node_attr = {
    "fontsize": "13",
    "fontname": "Arial",
    "margin": "0.4"
}

edge_attr = {
    "fontsize": "11",
    "fontname": "Arial",
    "minlen": "1",        # Added to control minimum edge length
    "labelangle": "0",    # Added to control label angle
    "labeldistance": "1.0", # Added to control label distance
    "labelfloat": "false"  # Added to prevent label floating
}

try:
    # Create diagram with enhanced configuration
    with Diagram(
        "AWS Serverless Real-Time Anomaly Detection",
        filename="serverless_anomaly_detection",
        show=False,
        direction="LR",
        graph_attr=graph_attr,
        node_attr=node_attr,
        edge_attr=edge_attr,
        outformat="png"
    ):

        # External Users/Systems
        with Cluster("External Users & Systems"):
            users = Mobile("End Users")
            
        # AWS Account boundary with enhanced visibility
        with Cluster("AWS Account\nServerless Anomaly Detection System"):
            # Frontend/UI Layer for user interaction
            with Cluster("Frontend Layer"):
                ui = Amplify("Web UI\n(AWS Amplify)")
                cdn = CloudFront("Content\nDelivery")

            # Data Ingestion Layer for real-time data processing
            with Cluster("Data Ingestion Layer"):
                kinesis = KinesisDataStreams("Real-time\nData Streams")

            # Processing Layer with Lambda functions
            with Cluster("Serverless Processing Layer"):
                preprocessing_lambda = Lambda("Data\nPreprocessing")
                anomaly_lambda = Lambda("Anomaly\nDetection")
                notification_lambda = Lambda("Alert\nNotification")

            # Storage Layer for data persistence
            with Cluster("Storage Layer"):
                dynamodb = Dynamodb("Historical Data\n& Thresholds")
                model_artifacts = S3("ML Model\nArtifacts")

            # Machine Learning Layer for model inference
            with Cluster("Machine Learning Layer"):
                sagemaker = SagemakerModel("SageMaker\nEndpoints")

            # Monitoring Layer for system observability
            with Cluster("Monitoring Layer"):
                cloudwatch = Cloudwatch("CloudWatch\nMetrics & Logs")

            # Notification Layer for alerts
            with Cluster("Notification Layer"):
                sns = SNS("SNS\nAlerts")

            # Security Layer
            with Cluster("Security Layer"):
                iam = IAM("IAM Roles\n& Policies")

            # User Interface Flow
            users >> Edge(color="blue", style="bold", label="HTTPS", minlen="0.5", labeldistance="0.5", labelangle="0", weight="2") >> cdn
            cdn >> Edge(color="blue", label="Serve UI") >> ui
            
            # Data Processing Flow
            kinesis >> Edge(color="green", style="bold", label="Stream Events", minlen="1", labeldistance="1.0") >> preprocessing_lambda
            preprocessing_lambda >> Edge(color="orange", label="Query History", minlen="0.5", labeldistance="0.5", labelangle="0", weight="2") >> dynamodb
            preprocessing_lambda >> Edge(color="green", label="Process Data", minlen="1", labeldistance="1.0") >> anomaly_lambda
            
            # Machine Learning Flow
            anomaly_lambda >> Edge(color="purple", style="bold", label="Inference", minlen="1", labeldistance="1.0") >> sagemaker
            sagemaker >> Edge(color="purple", style="dashed", label="Load Model", minlen="1", labeldistance="1.0") >> model_artifacts
            
            # Results and Notification Flow
            anomaly_lambda >> Edge(color="orange", label="Store Results", minlen="0.1", labeldistance="0.2", labelangle="0", weight="5") >> dynamodb
            anomaly_lambda >> Edge(color="red", label="Trigger Alert", minlen="1", labeldistance="1.0") >> notification_lambda
            notification_lambda >> Edge(color="red", style="bold", label="Push Alert", minlen="1", labeldistance="1.0") >> sns
            
            # Monitoring Connections (CloudWatch)
            cloudwatch - Edge(style="dotted", color="gray") - kinesis
            cloudwatch - Edge(style="dotted", color="gray") - preprocessing_lambda
            cloudwatch - Edge(style="dotted", color="gray") - anomaly_lambda
            cloudwatch - Edge(style="dotted", color="gray") - sagemaker
            
            # Security Connections (IAM)
            iam - Edge(style="dashed", color="darkred") - preprocessing_lambda
            iam - Edge(style="dashed", color="darkred") - anomaly_lambda
            iam - Edge(style="dashed", color="darkred") - notification_lambda
            
            # Alert Notification Flow
            sns >> Edge(color="red", style="bold", label="Email/SMS") >> users

except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error generating diagram: {str(e)}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)
